title: perf-incident-postmortem-slo-miss-customer-escalation-2026-04-12
content:
Summary:

On 2026-04-12 we observed sustained SLO misses for text-generation endpoints serving model rwd/gpt-small-v2 in the hosted API region us-west-2. The incident impacted a small set of high-QPS customers (notably Acme Corp) with increased p95 latency and elevated error surface related to request timeouts and transient 502 responses. This doc captures the detection timeline, profiling and benchmark findings, root-cause analysis, hotfix validation, customer communication, and follow-up actions.

Impact:
- Window: 2026-04-12 03:12 UTC — 2026-04-12 05:03 UTC (approx 1h 51m)
- Scope: ~4% of total requests to the rwd/gpt-small-v2 route in us-west-2; affected endpoints saw p95 latency increase from ~220ms to ~620ms and p99 from ~480ms to ~1.2s.
- Customer-visible: Timeouts (5s) and increased tail latency for real-time UX; one customer (Acme Corp) opened a support escalation at 03:25 UTC.
- Cost: transient spike in GPU utilization and autoscale-triggered additional slots; preliminary cost delta modest but notable given scale.

Detection and Response Timeline (high-level):
- 03:12 UTC: Alert fired - slo_latency_p95 > target for rwd/gpt-small-v2 in us-west-2 (Pager duty: Daniel Kim).
- 03:15 UTC: Incident declared; on-call team paged SRE and serving-runtime leads.
- 03:22 UTC: Customer escalation received from Acme (case #JIRA-3217).
- 03:28 UTC: Initial mitigation — roll forward config to increase max_batch_size from 8 to 16 for the affected fleet (quick attempt to improve throughput). No improvement.
- 03:40 UTC: Profiling started (perf traces, nvprof-like telemetry, kernel-level counters, and runtime metrics).
- 04:05 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis refined; small rollback of a runtime kernel selection change (PR 784) deployed to a portion of canary nodes. Observed improvement on canary nodes.
- 04:25 UTC: Hotfix rollout (rollback of PR 784) completed to the fleet in us-west-2.
- 04:40 UTC: Monitoring shows p95 returning to baseline; incident declared mitigated.
- 05:03 UTC: Incident closed after 20 minutes of stable metrics and customer confirmation.

Root cause analysis (summary):
Primary cause: Regression in kernel selection heuristics introduced in PR 784 (serving-runtime optimizer) that changed which CUDA kernels were selected for the fused attention path for sequence lengths commonly seen by rwd/gpt-small-v2. The new selection caused increased kernel launch overhead and poorer L2 cache locality for typical online sequence distributions, amplifying tail latency.
Contributing factors:
- Canary sampling was insufficiently representative: the canary workload had lower QPS and shorter sequence lengths (avg 32 tokens) compared to production (avg 64 tokens), which hid the regression.
- Autoscaling / batching interplay: an autoscale-triggered scale-up in the middle of the spike caused transient rebalancing and KV cache cold-starts for some nodes, worsening tail behavior during the regression window.
- Smoke tests lacked p95/p99 profiling for typical sequence-length histograms.

Profiling & forensic data (high-level):
- Kernel metrics (GPU): increased avg kernel launch latency by ~2.6x for attention kernels under production sequence distribution; L2 miss rate increased ~18%.
- CPU-side: scheduler wakeups increased due to longer GPU stalls; thread contention on IO dispatch queues grew by ~40%.
- Runtime traces: KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% during autoscale events; many requests experienced extra 1-2ms waiting for batch formation because kernel runtimes increased unpredictably.
- Benchmarks run during investigation (representative synthetic workload matching production token histogram):
  - Baseline (pre-PR 784): p50 120ms, p95 220ms, p99 480ms
  - Post-PR 784 (regressed): p50 160ms, p95 620ms, p99 1.2s
  - Post-rollback (hotfix): p50 118ms, p95 230ms, p99 490ms

Why the initial mitigation (increase max_batch_size) failed:
- The regression increased per-token kernel time; forcing larger batches only increased waiting time for first token in a batch and increased end-to-end latency for latency-sensitive requests. Larger batches improved throughput for long-running throughput tests but worsened tail latency for real-time traffic patterns.

Hotfix validation steps performed:
1) Deployed rollback of PR 784 to a 10% canary (nodes with production-like traffic) at 04:05 UTC.
2) Ran deterministic microbenchmarks (attention kernel microbench) and end-to-end synthetic traffic matching production sequence-length distribution; observed kernel metrics returning to baseline within 3 minutes on canary.
3) Gradual rollout to 100% in us-west-2 with health checks that verify slo_latency_p95, kernel launch time, and KV cache hit-rate; automated rollback configured if any metric diverged by >15% from baseline.
4) Post-rollout smoke tests: ran a small A/B traffic split against Acme Corp traffic pattern; Acme confirmed improved UX at 04:58 UTC.

Customer communication:
- 03:30 UTC: Acknowledge to Acme support: "We are investigating elevated latencies and will provide updates every 30 minutes."
- 04:10 UTC: Update: "We identified a regression in a recent runtime optimization and have begun a controlled rollback to validate." (included PR link and JIRA case).
- 05:10 UTC: Resolution: "Full rollback completed; metrics returned to expected levels; please re-open the ticket if you observe any regression."

Action items and follow-ups (owners and ETA):
- Improve canary traffic fidelity: create a canary workload generator that mirrors production token length/QPS histograms. Owner: Priya Rao. ETA: 2026-04-30.
- Add kernel-selection regression tests: microbench harness that runs candidate kernel selections against multiple sequence-length distributions and collects p95/p99. Owner: Liam Chen. ETA: 2026-04-20.
- Revise autoscale cooldown & KV prewarm: ensure prewarm occurs before traffic is routed to new nodes; reduce churn that compounds regressions. Owner: Marcus Patel (SRE). ETA: 2026-05-05.
- Expand monitoring: add p99 kernel-launch-time and L2 miss-rate to critical SLO dashboards and automated runbook thresholds. Owner: Daniel Kim. ETA: 2026-04-18.
- Postmortem review with runtime and applied-ml teams to align kernel heuristics with model sequence distributions; schedule 1: 2026-04-16. Owner: Ava Martinez.

Mitigation proposals (longer term):
- Kernel selection audit: build a matrix of model families vs ideal kernel choices and test across sequence-length percentiles.
- Canary policy change: route a statistically significant sample of real traffic (including high-QPS customers) to canaries for a 30m soak before global rollout for runtime changes.
- Batching guardrails: implement adaptive batch-size heuristics that prioritize latency SLOs for flagged low-latency routes.

Appendix (supporting artifacts):
- Perf traces and nvprof dumps: stored in s3://redwood-inference/perf-traces/2026-04-12/ (access via internal link).
- JIRA case: JIRA-3217 (customer escalation ticket).
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/784 (kernel-selection change).

Notes / open questions:
- Need to verify whether any other model families were exposed to the same kernel-selection logic and were protected by different canary coverage. Preliminary scan shows rwd/gpt-medium-v1 did not regress because of different seq-length distribution.
- Investigate whether autoscaler placement decisions (mix of new vs old nodes) can be tuned to reduce cache cold-starts during rollouts.

Prepared by: Ava Martinez (serving-runtime lead)
Reviewed by: Daniel Kim, Priya Rao

End of document.
